THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING - B GROUP, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:5256  WP No.101220 of 2024  ORDER

The petitioners are seeking issuance of writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to finalize and pass the award forthwith and pay the reasonable compensation pursuant to the final notification issued by respondent No.4 dated 13.11.2022 and to consider the representations of the petitioners dated 16.12.2023 submitted to the respondents vide Annexures-E, F, G, H, J and K.
2.

Heard Sri Sangamesh S.Ghulappanavar, learned counsel for the petitioners, Smt.Kirtilata R.Patil,
learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent Nos.1 to 4, 6 & 7 and Sri Chetan Munnoli,
learned counsel for respondent No.5 3.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that, the petitioners are the owners of the land.
A notification was issued for acquisition of his land for Upper Krishna Project.

Final notification under Section 19 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land NC: 2024:KHC-D:5256 Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 ("the Act, 2013" for short) was issued on 13.11.2022, but the award is not yet passed.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land NC: 2024:KHC-D:5256 Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As per Section 25 of the Act 2013, the period within which the award is to be made is 12 months from the date of publication of the declaration under Section 19 of the Act, 2013.
The Section further says that, if no award is made within that period, the entire proceedings for acquisition of the land shall lapse.

4. Learned counsel submitted that, the first proviso to Section 25 of the Act, 2013 enables the appropriate Government to extend the period of 12 months, if in its opinion circumstances exist justifying the same.
But as per the second proviso decision to extent the period shall be recorded in writing, the same shall be notified and shall be uploaded in the Website of the authorities concerned.
But no such extension is made in the present case.
Therefore prays for allowing the petitioner.
Learned High Court Government Pleader has not addressed the argument as she has not received any instructions from the respondents.
Sufficient time is already given to secure instructions and to address the argument.
Hence, her argument is taken as nil.

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that the petitioners are the owners of the land which was notified for acquisition for Upper Krishna project.
Notification produced as per Annexure-B under Section 19 of the Act, 2013 was passed on 13.11.2022.
It is also not in dispute that the award is not passed till today.

As per Section 19 of the Act, 2013 after publication of declaration and summary of rehabilitation and settlement, when the property is required for public purpose, the final notification is to be published as per Section 25 of the Act, 2013.
The Collector shall make an award within a period of 12 months from the date of such publication of declaration under Section 19 of the Act, 2013.
If no such award is made within a period of 12 months, the entire proceedings for acquisition NC: 2024:KHC-D:5256 of the land shall lapse.

Even though the Government is authorised to extend the period of 12 months as per the proviso to Section 25 of the Act, 2013, such extension shall be in writing and shall be notified and to be uploaded on the website of the authority concerned.
But it is not the contention taken by the respondents that there was any extension of period.
There cannot be any justification for the respondents for not passing the award when the notification under Section 19 of the Act, 2013 was published on 13.11.2022.
However, the petitioner is not seeking the declaration that the entire proceedings for acquisition of the land has already lapsed.
The prayer is for issuance of writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondent to pass award forthwith and to pay reasonable compensation.
7. The materials on record also disclose that the petitioners have submitted various representations to all the respondents, but it has not given any relief to the petitioners.
Therefore I am of the opinion that the NC: 2024:KHC-D:5256 petitioners are entitled for the relief as claimed.
Hence, the petition is liable to be allowed.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The writ petition is allowed.

Respondent Nos.4, 6 and 7 are directed to pass award determining the just and reasonable compensation payable to the petitioners within 45 days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Failing which, the petitioner is entitled to take further action in accordance with law.
